ruling.recommended_action: Send to a human reviewer: confirm from the driver's app / Balestier Rd trace whether the 21:26–21:37 segment was driven on Balestier Road; if the correspondence cannot be established, the segment is unexempted and the refund follows the RD-2 formula (4.89 km × $1.4098/km = $6.89). No account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a metered RydeTAXI trip (base $3.90, distance $23.84, time $7.35, waiting $0.11, platform $1.47, total $36.67 [F7]), so any unexplained off-route distance enters the fare through the meter [RD-2]. Both parties agree the trip is metered and that only unbilled route distance units, not the whole fare, can be refunded [F4][F7][RD-2].

The record settles that a deviation occurred and that no traffic-cause exemption applies. The single off-route segment ran 21:26–21:37, driving 6.64 km where the optimal route covers 1.76 km, adding 4.89 km and straying up to 2070 m from the optimal route [F3]; overall the trip ran 16.9 km against an optimal 11.6 km (+5.3 km, +46%) [F1][F2]. No traffic incident was recorded near the route during the trip window [F15] and the weather was fair [F16], so RD-4(a) is unavailable; the Central Expressway band 2 reading (10–19 km/h, 21:06–21:26) is corroboration at most and cannot exempt a segment on its own [F12][RD-4].

The one open question is the scope of the rider's agreement. The driver asked at 21:23 "Jam on Central Expressway is building up ahead, can I go round via Balestier Road?" [F8] and the rider replied at 21:24 "Can lah, go ahead." [F9] inside a complete, fully timestamped chat record [F10]. That is a rider message sent before the segment started [F3][F9][RD-5], so consent to a named road — Balestier Road — is established, and the timing requirement of "before you go" is met (the driver's post-trip statement [F11] adds nothing, since a driver's own claim is not consent [RD-5]). What is not established is whether the driven segment was that road: no chat message, stop or fare/gps fact places the car on Balestier Road, and the road names in the record (Central Expressway, Bishan Street 11, Braddell Road) appear only as speed-band readings [F13][F14], not as the driven path. Under RD-5 a specific named-road agreement covers driving on X only and the record must tie the segment to X; timing alone does not [RD-5]. This is exactly the reading both advocates put forward (named_road_untied), so the segment's scope is undetermined and no exemption executes on it [F3][F8][F9][RD-5].

The finding changes the amount, so it cannot be left undetermined: with the segment undetermined the case must go to a human rather than execute a refund, since the trace's formula would otherwise be 4.89 km × $1.4098/km (this trip's distance fare ÷ distance km) = $6.89 [F3][F4][RD-2]. No account flag: neither party has an upheld route dispute in the last 90 days, so RD-6's repeated-breach threshold is not met [F17][F18][RD-6]. The $0.11 metered waiting unit (0.4 min) is properly charged under RD-3(c) and is not in dispute [F5][F7][RD-3].

segment_findings.reason: The rider's own message at 21:24 ('Can lah, go ahead.', F9) answered the driver's 21:23 ask naming Balestier Road (F8) and came before the 21:26 segment start, so consent to a named road exists [RD-5]. But consent to a named road covers driving on that road only, and the record ties nothing to Balestier Road: no stop, no positioning message, no road name in any gps, timeline or fare fact — the road names present (Central Expressway, Bishan Street 11, Braddell Road) are speed-band readings only [F3][F13][F14][RD-5]. Timing alone does not tie the segment to the agreed road [RD-5]; the segment is therefore undetermined and the case goes to a human.

rejected_claims.reason: The rider argues the unmatched named-road consent makes the segment unexempted, so it 'stands' as a refundable detour [F3][F9][RD-5]. RD-5/G13 provides the opposite consequence for a specific named-road agreement with no correspondence record: the finding is undetermined, not counts, so no refund executes on this record [F3][F8][F9][RD-5].

The requested refund of $6.89 (4.89 km × $1.4098/km) assumes the segment is unexempted [F3][F4][RD-2]. Because the segment's scope is undetermined rather than unexempted, the amount cannot be executed and the case is escalated [F3][F9][RD-5].

Claimed the driver profile shows 0 upheld disputes in 90 days [F17][F18]. Accepted only as far as it goes: the RD-6 flag threshold is not met, but this does not bear on whether the segment is exempt, which is decided under RD-5 [F3][F18][RD-6].

The driver argues the absence of any record tying the segment to Balestier Road (or to anywhere else) means it 'cannot be treated as an unexplained deviation' [F3][F8][F9][RD-5]. No correspondence record defeats an exemption, it produces an undetermined finding, which does not convert the measured 6.64 km / +4.89 km segment into an exempt one [F3][RD-1][RD-5].

The driver invokes the Central Expressway band 2 reading as reasonable-cause context for the reroute [F12][F3][RD-4]. A speed-band record alone does not exempt; RD-4(a) requires an incident, and none was recorded near the route [F12][F15][RD-4].
